warnings: Regular 1-in-6 pulldown detected (16% repeated frames); dropped 12 duplicate frames and adjusted FPS from 29.97 to 25.17 unique fps.
Effective unique frame rate is 25.2 fps (~91.4 deg arm sweep/frame); release-instant kinematics carry elevated temporal quantization error.

calibration_notes: Closed-form Two-Wicket calibration (MCC Laws 6 & 8): f=10208 px (FOV_max=10.7 deg), Z_near=24.7 m, cam_height=1.42 m, pitch=-1.35 deg, roll=0.00 deg.
Camera motion/pan detected: Two-Wicket focal length K and vertical gravity are calibrated (passed directly into NLF), while ground-referenced translation metrics remain gated.

runup_speed_mps.label: Run-Up Approach Speed
runup_speed_mps.suppression_reason: Suppressed: world-grounded translation requires a static camera with calibrated MCC pitch/wicket geometry; camera pan or uncalibrated FOV distorts depth displacement.
runup_speed_mps.definition_note: Mean horizontal pelvis velocity (+X) over [BFC - 220 ms, BFC] in calibrated Pitch World.
runup_speed_mps.empirical_reference: Elite male fast bowlers (n=20): 5.83 +- 0.50 m/s (strongest pace predictor: +0.89 m/s ball speed per SD).
runup_speed_mps.literature_source: Worthington, King, & Ranson (2013), J. Applied Biomechanics; Felton et al. (2019)

stride_length_pct_stature.label: Delivery Stride Length
stride_length_pct_stature.suppression_reason: Suppressed: world-grounded translation requires a static camera with calibrated MCC pitch/wicket geometry; camera pan or uncalibrated FOV distorts depth displacement.
stride_length_pct_stature.definition_note: Horizontal pitch-axis displacement X_front_ankle(FFC) - X_rear_ankle(BFC) divided by estimated stature.
stride_length_pct_stature.empirical_reference: Published adult fast-bowling stride length: ~75-88% of stature (1.35-1.65 m).
stride_length_pct_stature.literature_source: Portus et al. (2004); Worthington et al. (2013)

front_knee_ffc_deg.label: Front Knee Angle at FFC
front_knee_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
front_knee_ffc_deg.definition_note: 3D internal hip-knee-ankle angle at FFC (180 deg = fully straight; Rician out-of-plane debiased).
front_knee_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Typical adult fast-bowling FFC angle: ~150-170 deg (180 deg = straight).

front_knee_br_deg.label: Front Knee Angle at Ball Release
front_knee_br_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
front_knee_br_deg.definition_note: 3D internal hip-knee-ankle angle at BR (180 deg = fully straight; Rician out-of-plane debiased).
front_knee_br_deg.empirical_reference: Elite male fast bowlers (n=20): straighter front knee at BR strongly predicts speed (+0.79 m/s per SD).
front_knee_br_deg.literature_source: Worthington, King, & Ranson (2013), J. Applied Biomechanics

front_knee_change_deg.label: Front Knee Bracing Change (FFC->BR)
front_knee_change_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
front_knee_change_deg.empirical_reference: Extender/braced patterns generally conserve braking impulse better than collapsing flexors.

trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.label: Global Trunk Forward Inclination at FFC
trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.definition_note: Global-vertical sagittal inclination atan2(sx, sy) of pelvis->neck vector (proxy; differs from Worthington inter-segment trunk angle).
trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Global trunk inclination proxy (not directly interchangeable with Worthington upper-vs-lower trunk angle).
trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.literature_source: Global Pitch-Frame Proxy (cf. Worthington et al., 2013)

trunk_flexion_br_deg.label: Global Trunk Forward Inclination at BR
trunk_flexion_br_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
trunk_flexion_br_deg.definition_note: Global-vertical sagittal inclination atan2(sx, sy) of pelvis->neck vector at BR.
trunk_flexion_br_deg.empirical_reference: Global trunk inclination proxy at release (not directly interchangeable with inter-segment trunk flexion).
trunk_flexion_br_deg.literature_source: Global Pitch-Frame Proxy (cf. Worthington et al., 2013)

trunk_flexion_delta_deg.label: Global Trunk Forward Flexion Change (FFC->BR)
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.definition_note: Change in global sagittal trunk inclination from FFC to BR (proxy for Worthington upper-trunk flexion).
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.empirical_reference: Greater forward trunk flexion FFC->BR associates with faster ball speeds (+0.58 m/s per SD in Worthington 2013).
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.literature_source: Global Pitch-Frame Proxy (cf. Worthington et al., 2013)

thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg.label: Global Trunk Contralateral Inclination at FFC
thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg.definition_note: Exact Z-X Cardan global contralateral tilt atan2(-sign_arm*sz, hypot(sx, sy)) of pelvis->neck vector at FFC.
thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Whole-trunk global lateral inclination at FFC (distinct from Alway 2021 thoracolumbar joint angle).

thorax_lat_flex_br_deg.label: Global Trunk Contralateral Inclination at BR
thorax_lat_flex_br_deg.definition_note: Exact Z-X Cardan global contralateral tilt of pelvis->neck vector at BR. Note: Bayne (2016) studied 25 adolescents (14-19 y: 50+-6 vs 40+-8 deg); Alway (2021) elite adults found injured bowlers were LESS side-flexed at BR (thoracolumbar 17 vs 20 deg).
thorax_lat_flex_br_deg.empirical_reference: Context-dependent: adolescent cohort (Bayne 2016, n=25) vs elite adult study (Alway 2021, n=50) disagree in direction; interpret alongside workload.
thorax_lat_flex_br_deg.literature_source: Bayne et al. (2016) [adolescent cohort]; Alway et al. (2021) [elite adults]

pelvis_alignment_bfc_deg.label: Pelvis Alignment at BFC
pelvis_alignment_bfc_deg.definition_note: Unwrapped horizontal pelvis line angle relative to +X pitch axis (180=side-on, 270=front-on).
pelvis_alignment_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: AIS convention (Portus et al. 2001): <210 deg side-on, 210-240 deg semi-open, >240 deg front-on.
pelvis_alignment_bfc_deg.literature_source: Portus et al. (2001/2004), ISBS / Sports Biomechanics

shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.label: Shoulder Alignment at BFC
shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.definition_note: Unwrapped horizontal shoulder line angle relative to +X pitch axis (anchored to pelvis branch at BFC).
shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: AIS convention (Portus et al. 2001): <210 deg side-on, 210-240 deg semi-open, >240 deg front-on.
shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.literature_source: Portus et al. (2001/2004), ISBS / Sports Biomechanics

shoulder_counter_rotation_deg.label: Shoulder Counter-Rotation (SCR, BFC->FFC)
shoulder_counter_rotation_deg.empirical_reference: AIS mixed-action threshold >=30 deg (Portus 2001/2004 retrospective); note Alway (2021) prospective adult study found no SCR-LBSI link.
shoulder_counter_rotation_deg.literature_source: Portus et al. (2001/2004) [retrospective]; Alway et al. (2021) [no prospective link]

hip_shoulder_sep_bfc_deg.label: Hip-Shoulder Separation at BFC
hip_shoulder_sep_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: AIS mixed-action criterion includes |separation at BFC| >= 30 deg.

max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.label: Peak Dynamic Hip-Shoulder Separation
max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.definition_note: Peak pelvis-minus-shoulder separation across [BFC, BR] (10 Hz filtered).
max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.empirical_reference: Descriptive transverse torso twist measure across the delivery stride.
max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.literature_source: Portus et al. (2004); Worthington et al. (2013)

delayed_arm_ffc_deg.label: Bowling Arm Behind Global Vertical at FFC
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: effective rate is 25.2 fps (~91 deg/frame); high-velocity arm kinematics require >=100 fps (ideally 120-240 fps).
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.definition_note: Angle of bowling upper arm behind global vertical (+Y) at FFC (global proxy for Worthington shoulder-to-trunk angle 331+-22 deg).
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Larger arm delay at FFC strongly predicts faster pace (+0.62 m/s per SD in Worthington 2013).
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.literature_source: Global Pitch-Frame Proxy (cf. Worthington et al., 2013)

rear_hip_bfc_deg.label: Rear Hip Angle Proxy at BFC (Trunk-to-Thigh)
rear_hip_bfc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
rear_hip_bfc_deg.definition_note: 3D angle between upward trunk (neck-pelv) and rear thigh (rkne-rhip) at BFC (proxy; Alway 2021 measured 3D pelvis-to-thigh segment angle: 146+-10 deg LBSI vs 156+-9 deg uninjured).
rear_hip_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: Proxy for Alway (2021) rear-hip predictor (more flexed rear hip at BFC associated with LBSI in 50-bowler study).
rear_hip_bfc_deg.literature_source: Trunk-Thigh Proxy (cf. Alway et al., 2021, MSSE)

pelvic_drop_ffc_deg.label: Frontal Pelvic Tilt at FFC
pelvic_drop_ffc_deg.definition_note: Coronal angle of hip line (rear_hip_y - front_hip_y) at FFC.
pelvic_drop_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Frontal-plane pelvic control indicator during front-foot braking.

non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.label: Non-Bowling (Front) Arm Elevation at FFC
non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (0 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.definition_note: Elevation of non-bowling upper arm above horizontal at FFC.
non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Descriptive front-arm position entering front-foot contact.

peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.label: Peak Bowling Arm Angular Velocity
peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.suppression_reason: Suppressed: effective rate is 25.2 fps (~91 deg/frame); high-velocity arm kinematics require >=100 fps (ideally 120-240 fps).
peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.definition_note: Peak Savitzky-Golay (~50 ms) angular velocity of bowling upper arm during [FFC, BR].
peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.empirical_reference: High-speed kinematic descriptor; requires >=100 fps and verified timebase.

release_height_m.label: Ball Release Height (Local Ground)
release_height_m.definition_note: Vertical wrist height at BR above local front-ankle ground reference during [FFC, BR].

follow_through_drift_deg.label: Follow-Through Lateral Drift Angle
follow_through_drift_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: world-grounded translation requires a static camera with calibrated MCC pitch/wicket geometry; camera pan or uncalibrated FOV distorts depth displacement.
follow_through_drift_deg.definition_note: Lateral-to-forward pelvis travel angle over [BR, BR+250 ms] (requires static calibrated world translation).
follow_through_drift_deg.empirical_reference: Requires calibrated static-camera world translation; suppressed under panning or uncalibrated FOV.

icc_elbow_legality_verdict.label: ICC 15-Degree Elbow Extension Legality
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.suppression_reason: PERMANENTLY REFUSED ON VIDEO: Accredited ICC bowling legality adjudication requires >=250 Hz multi-camera 3D optical motion capture with anatomical upper-arm/forearm marker clusters. Abraham, Feros, & Fox (2025, IJSSC) reported 22.71 deg elbow RMSE even on three calibrated 240 Hz iPads.
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.definition_note: Permanent scientific refusal per ICC testing regulations.
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.empirical_reference: ICC limit: <=15 deg elbow extension from Upper Arm Horizontal (UAH) to Ball Release (BR).
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.literature_source: ICC Illegal Bowling Action Regulations; Abraham, Feros, & Fox (2025), IJSSC 20(6)

cohort_comparisons.label: Global Trunk Contralateral Inclination at BR
cohort_comparisons.definition_note: Whole-trunk global tilt proxy. Note: Bayne (2016) studied adolescents (injured 50+-6 vs uninjured 40+-8); Alway (2021) adult study found injured bowlers LESS side-flexed at BR.
cohort_comparisons.source: Bayne et al. (2016) [adolescents]; Alway et al. (2021) [adults]

cohort_comparisons.label: Shoulder Counter-Rotation (SCR, BFC->FFC)
cohort_comparisons.definition_note: AIS mixed-action threshold is >=30 deg (retrospective link in Portus 2004; no prospective LBSI link in Alway 2021).
cohort_comparisons.source: Portus et al. (2001/2004); Alway et al. (2021)

kinetic_efficiency.status_label: Retired (Unvalidated Composite — See Verified Metrics & Cohort Norms)
kinetic_efficiency.summary: 0-100 composite scores are retired until validated against external ground-truth outcomes (0/5 underlying metrics observable).

lumbar_load_screening.name: Mechanical Load & Durability Screening
lumbar_load_screening.status_label: Retired (Unvalidated Composite — See Verified Metrics & Cohort Norms)
lumbar_load_screening.summary: 0-100 composite scores are retired until validated against external ground-truth outcomes (4/5 underlying metrics observable).

quadrant.interpretation: Composite 2D quadrant placement is disabled until underlying metrics are calibrated against external biomechanical & workload outcomes.

limiters.title: Mixed-Action Shoulder Counter-Rotation (>=30 deg)
limiters.biomechanical_mechanism: Shoulder counter-rotation (46.2 deg, interval [36.9, 55.0]) strictly clears the 30-degree AIS mixed-action threshold (Portus 2001/2004 retrospective; note Alway 2021 prospective adult study did not find an independent SCR-LBSI association).
limiters.actionable_recommendation: Align hips and shoulders coherently at BFC to minimize abrupt upper-trunk recoil.

capture_upgrades.title: Switch Smartphone to 120–240 fps Slow-Motion
capture_upgrades.biomechanical_mechanism: Effective unique rate is 25.2 fps (~91 deg arm sweep/frame).
capture_upgrades.actionable_recommendation: Record outdoors in native 1080p 240 fps slow-motion.

capture_upgrades.title: Lock Camera on a Static Tripod (Eliminate Handheld Pan)
capture_upgrades.biomechanical_mechanism: Pitch intrinsics were calibrated from visible wickets/creases, but handheld camera panning prevents reliable world-frame pelvis translation, stride length, and follow-through drift.
capture_upgrades.actionable_recommendation: Lock the tripod head during the delivery so background wickets stay stationary.

capture_upgrades.title: Add a Side-On (90 deg) Camera Angle
capture_upgrades.biomechanical_mechanism: Rear/front cameras cannot accurately resolve sagittal front-knee bracing or trunk flexion.
capture_upgrades.actionable_recommendation: Place a tripod phone 8-12 m perpendicular to the popping crease showing full body.

hard_guardrails: ICC 15-degree elbow legality CANNOT be adjudicated from monocular or casual 2D/3D video; accredited >=250 Hz 3D optical lab testing is required.
Biomechanical load screening estimates single-delivery mechanical posture only and is NOT a medical diagnosis; injury risk depends strongly on workload, age/skeletal maturity, and physical capacity.
Intervals reported without held-out physical reference calibration represent repeatability or analytical sensitivity estimates rather than externally calibrated laboratory confidence intervals.
